blocks.text: An **array** holds a fixed number of values of the same type: the type is `[N]T`, that is `N` values of `T`. The length is known at compile time. You reach an element with `array[i]` (counting starts at 0) and get the length with `.len`. `[0; 100]` builds an array of a hundred zeros.
An index out of bounds stops the program at run time; it never silently writes to the wrong place in memory. With **`type`** you can give a long type a short name.
